settings.text: A pillow cover is the easiest way to keep a pillow fresh. Wash the cover often and give the pillow itself a little air.
settings.note: General guidance. This is general advice for caring for cotton, cotton satin and polyester fills. It is not specific to one product. Always follow the care label on your item first.

settings.heading: Everyday care
settings.text:
• Use a pillow cover, and wash it with your sheets.
  • Plump your pillows each morning to keep the filling even.
  • Air them now and then in fresh air, out of strong direct sun.

settings.heading: Cleaning
settings.text:
• Spot-clean small marks with a damp cloth and a little mild detergent.
  • Only machine wash a filled pillow if its care label allows it. Wash two at a time to keep the drum balanced.
  • Use a gentle cycle and rinse well.

settings.heading: Drying
settings.text:
• Dry pillows completely before you use them. Damp filling can clump and smell musty.
  • If the label allows a dryer, use a low heat and plump the pillows between cycles.

settings.heading: When to replace
settings.text:
• Fold the pillow in half. If it stays folded instead of springing back, the filling has lost its support.
  • Lumps that will not plump out are another sign.

settings.question: How often should I wash pillow covers?
settings.answer: Many people wash them once a week, with the sheets, or more often in hot weather.

settings.question: Can I wash the pillows themselves?
settings.answer: Only if the care label allows it. Otherwise spot-clean and air them, and keep them in a cover.
